summary: Normanook-named state fire tower in Stokes State Forest, first used in 1908; present Aermotor tower dated 1933 or 1934 (sources differ); staffed in fall and spring per a 2021 account.

facts.design: Aermotor tower, 47 feet with a 7x7 foot cab per NHLR (Willhite says 45 feet)

staffing.status: Manned by NJ Forest Fire Service during the fall and spring

access.note: On foot via the Appalachian Trail corridor; a locked gate keeps motor vehicles off the fire road except for authorized people

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot from the Appalachian Trail corridor in Stokes State Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says first used in 1908 and NHLR says established in 1908 under the Normanook name. Willhite dates the first state tower to 1918 with a start-up in April 1919. The story gives both.
NHLR dates the present Aermotor tower to 1933; Willhite says a CCC-built tower went up in 1934. Not resolved; the story gives both dates.
Wikipedia and NHLR give 47 feet (14 m); Willhite gives 45 feet. The story says roughly 45 to 47 feet.

sources.title: List of New Jersey Forest Fire Service fire towers

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: first use 1908 (Wikipedia, NHLR) vs first state tower 1918 with April 1919 start-up (Willhite); present tower 1933 (NHLR) vs CCC tower 1934 (Willhite). Not settled. A Takeahike.us page search result also gives 1933 and an Aermotor attribution; it was not opened and is not cited. Staffing and gate details come from NHLR visitor comments (one dated visit report, August 6, 2018) and from Willhite's 2021 account. Willhite is a personal hiking site. Do not encourage climbing: this is a manned working lookout. Brief height 14 m and Sussex County are consistent with sources; no corrections.
